categories.name: Lint Violations
categories.description: lake lint's defsWithUnderscore linter flags two new theorem-like `def`s introduced by task 180 in Theorems.lean. Both declarations are `noncomputable def`s (not `theorem`/`lemma`, since they return a data-carrying `DerivationTree`), and CSLib's established convention for such DerivationTree-returning defs elsewhere in this same task's diff (e.g. `tempKDistDerived`, `pastKDist` in GeneralizedNecessitation.lean) already uses lowerCamelCase without underscores. These two new names break that established local convention.

violations.description: `def allFuture_iff_neg_someFuture_neg` contains underscores; mathlib convention requires lowerCamelCase for `def` declarations (underscores are only idiomatic for `theorem`/`lemma`).
violations.fix_hint: Rename to lowerCamelCase, e.g. `allFutureIffNegSomeFutureNeg`, and update all call sites (Chronicle/TruthLemma.lean references `mcs_allFuture_iff`, not this def directly — but check for any other references).

violations.description: `def allPast_iff_neg_somePast_neg` contains underscores; same issue as above (past dual).
violations.fix_hint: Rename to lowerCamelCase, e.g. `allPastIffNegSomePastNeg`, and update all call sites.

categories.name: Proof Completeness / Honesty
categories.description: A live (non-comment) `sorry` exists in `temporal_valid_of_bimodal_derivable` in TemporalConservativity.lean, guarded by `set_option warn.sorry false in`. This is thoroughly documented in the module docstring (module 'Domain Mismatch Resolution' section explains the AddCommGroup vs. arbitrary-serial-linear-order gap and two candidate resolution strategies) and is NOT one of the four intended bridge Axiom constructors — it is a genuine open proof obligation. This is honest/disclosed per CONTRIBUTING.md's spirit (documented rather than hidden), but it means `bimodal_conservative_over_temporal` (the main conservativity theorem) is not yet a complete, sorry-free proof. Distinct from the FMP-blocked `sorry`s in Tableau/Completeness.lean, which are all inside markdown code-fence comments (verified: only 4 occurrences of the literal token `sorry` outside comments were checked; Tableau/Completeness.lean's are all in commented-out ```lean blocks documenting blocked obligations, not live code).

violations.description: `temporal_valid_of_bimodal_derivable` ends in `sorry`, gated by `set_option warn.sorry false in` to suppress the build warning. The gap (AddCommGroup-domain soundness vs. arbitrary-serial-linear-order completeness) is well documented but unresolved, so `bimodal_conservative_over_temporal` transitively depends on this sorry.
violations.fix_hint: Either (a) prove the model-transfer result described in the 'Domain Mismatch Resolution' docstring section (order-isomorphism from ChronicleSubtype to a domain with AddCommGroup, or a direct satisfaction-preservation argument), or (b) if genuinely blocked, ensure the task's PR description discloses this remaining sorry explicitly (per AI/limitations disclosure norms) rather than leaving it implicit in code comments only.

categories.name: Documentation / Citation Hygiene
categories.description: Several Temporal metalogic module docstrings cite 'Burgess 1982' / 'Burgess (1982)' in plain prose without the bracket `[Description][BibKey]` citation format used elsewhere in this same task's diff (e.g. Formula.lean's `[H. Kamp, ...][Kamp1968]`, `[D. Gabbay, A. Pnueli, S. Shelah, J. Stavi, ...][GPSS1980]`). `references.bib` contains two distinct 1982 Burgess entries — `Burgess1982I` ('Since'/'Until') and `Burgess1982II` ('Time Periods') — and only `RRelation.lean` disambiguates which paper it means (matching `Burgess1982II`'s title in prose). The other three citing files do not specify I vs II, leaving the citation ambiguous even though the correct bib entries exist.

violations.standard: CONTRIBUTING.md (Documentation: 'reference the resource in your documentation')
violations.description: '* Burgess 1982: Section 2, Claim 2.11' does not use bracket-BibKey format and does not disambiguate Burgess1982I vs Burgess1982II.
violations.fix_hint: Change to '* [J. Burgess, Axioms for Tense Logic II: Time Periods][Burgess1982II]' (Claim 2.11 corresponds to the 'Time Periods' paper per RRelation.lean's citation of the same source's Lemmas 2.2-2.5).

violations.description: In-body docstring reference to 'Claim 2.11 of Burgess 1982' repeats the same ambiguity as line 34.
violations.fix_hint: Reference the disambiguated BibKey established at the top-of-file References section once fixed.

violations.description: '* Burgess (1982) — BX axiom system' does not disambiguate I vs II or use bracket-BibKey format.
violations.fix_hint: Disambiguate and use bracket format, e.g. '* [J. Burgess, Axioms for Tense Logic I/II][Burgess1982I][Burgess1982II]' if the BX system draws on both papers, or pick the specific one.

violations.description: '- Burgess (1982): BX axiom system for temporal logic' has the same ambiguity/format inconsistency.

violations.severity_note: Lowest priority of the five — already correctly disambiguates (II, 'Time Periods') in prose, just not in bracket-BibKey format.
violations.description: '* Burgess 1982: "Axioms for tense logic II: Time periods"' correctly identifies the paper but does not use the bracket-BibKey format used elsewhere in the same diff.
violations.fix_hint: Change to '* [J. Burgess, Axioms for Tense Logic II: Time Periods][Burgess1982II]' for consistency with Formula.lean's citation style.
